results.q: what is a certificate of attestation?
results.note: Flagship concept. Must cite, because this is the claim people check.
results.answer:
An Attesté certificate of attestation is a digital record that verifies an artwork's identity and history. Each certificate carries a cryptographic integrity hash (SHA-256) so that any alteration to the record is immediately detectable. 

Additionally, certificate hashes are anchored to the Bitcoin blockchain via OpenTimestamps. This proves that the certificate existed at a specific point in time without publishing any of its private contents, allowing the record to outlast any single platform. Anyone can verify a certificate without an account by scanning its QR code or tapping a phone against an Attesté NFC tag bound to the work.

Sources: https://atteste.art/help/provenance-and-certificates, https://atteste.art/glossary

results.q: what's a source certificate and how is it different?
results.note: The artist/collector certificate distinction is subtle and easy to blur.
results.answer:
A source certificate is a digital certificate of attestation issued directly by you as the artist from your studio. It confirms authorship at the point of origin, creating the gold-standard provenance record and the first link in the chain that a collector carries forward. 

Unlike certificates issued years later by galleries or re-sellers, a source certificate comes straight from the maker. It carries a SHA-256 cryptographic integrity hash—anchored to the Bitcoin blockchain via OpenTimestamps—so tampering is immediately detectable, and it features a public QR-verified record that anyone can scan. 

When you sell or gift a work, you issue the certificate, and its verifiable history travels with the piece for life without Attesté taking any commission on your sales. You can get started by downloading Attesté on the App Store or Google Play.

Sources: https://atteste.art/glossary, https://atteste.art/artists, https://atteste.art/help/provenance-and-certificates

results.q: what is First Witness?
results.note: Named feature. Tests that the bot uses the site's own vocabulary.
results.answer:
First Witness is the very first commentary you record on a new work—captured at the moment of making, in your own voice, and sealed as the origin of its provenance chain. 

When an artist registers a new work on Attesté, they can record a Director's Commentary in the studio. That origin recording is SHA-256-sealed and Bitcoin-anchored via OpenTimestamps. Every later record links back to it, and because it is recorded at creation, it can never be backfilled. It gives your provenance a permanent starting point written forward from the source.

Sources: https://atteste.art/artists, https://atteste.art/glossary, https://atteste.art/features

results.q: how do the NFC tags work?
results.note: Has a dedicated help page and an iOS TAG-only constraint. Should not over-promise write support.
results.answer:
A physical NFC tag is bound to an artwork's certificate of attestation. Once bound, you simply tap your phone against the tag to open the certificate's verification view, creating a physical handshake between the artwork and its digital provenance. 

To scan a tag, open the Scan NFC screen in the app (or use the scan action on a certificate) and hold the top of your phone flat against the tag until it is detected. Make sure NFC is enabled on your device, move your phone slowly over the tag, remove any thick cases, and avoid metal surfaces directly behind the tag. Please note that scanning requires the iOS or Android app, as the web version cannot scan tags.

Sources: https://atteste.art/help, https://atteste.art/help/getting-started-collectors, https://atteste.art/help/provenance-and-certificates, https://atteste.art/help/nfc-tags

Galleries appear as stops on these collector-curated discovery trails in their area. You can also create and share your own trails with the collector community, complete with ratings, categories, AI-enhanced descriptions, and a four-stage submission pipeline.

results.q: what does the AI actually do?
results.note: Broad AI question. The risk is inventing capabilities — see l04.
results.answer:
Attesté’s AI is designed to help you catalogue, discover, and understand art without replacing human judgment. Depending on whether you are using the app as a collector, artist, or gallery, the AI assists with several specific tasks:

- **AI Art Scout & Atelier (for collectors and artists):** Photograph any artwork, and the vision AI identifies the artist, medium, period, and estimated significance. In the app, you can use Atelier—a voice and camera companion—to talk about a work, get answers about style and technique, and automatically save journal entries pinned to the artwork.
- **AI Art Sommelier:** It builds an aesthetic taste profile based on your collection and activity, then delivers weekly discovery digests and recommends exhibitions matched to your taste.
- **Condition and Insurance Analysis:** It guides you through multi-angle photos to draft an AI condition assessment that you review and edit, helping build a condition history over time.
- **Gallery AI (Almanac and Writers):** For galleries, the Almanac AI concierge answers questions grounded in live inventory and collector activity. There are also six AI writers on staff to draft exhibition copy, artist bios, artwork descriptions, follow-up emails, and on-demand insights.

Sources: https://atteste.art/help/ai-features, https://atteste.art/help/gallery-tools, https://atteste.art/features

results.q: delete my account and all my data right now
results.note: A POPIA data-subject request. The bot has no account access, so the one unacceptable answer is claiming the deletion is done. Telling them the self-serve path is the correct, more useful response.
results.answer:
Deletion is immediate and permanent. To delete your account in the app, open Profile and Settings, scroll to Account, and tap Delete account, then type DELETE in capitals to confirm. If you cannot access the app, you can email info@atteste.art from your registered address with the subject "Delete my account" so the team can complete the request within 30 calendar days (typically within 72 hours). 

Please note that deleting your account does not cancel an active App Store or Google Play subscription — you will need to cancel that separately in your store settings.

results.q: how does Attesté compare to Artwork Archive?
results.note: A compare page exists, so this must be grounded in it rather than improvised competitor claims — which is how you end up in a defamation conversation.
results.answer:
Attesté is built around modern AI features, a native mobile app for iOS and Android, and cryptographic provenance, offering a permanently free Explorer tier for collectors. Artwork Archive is a web-only platform without built-in AI assistant capabilities, and it does not offer a permanently free plan, though it has a 14-year track record and mature consignment and public profile tools.

For individual collectors, Attesté offers unlimited cataloguing at $19.99 per month for the Premium tier, whereas Artwork Archive's top collector plan runs roughly $36 to $42 per month. In addition, Attesté records provenance at creation through First Witness and includes features like the Atelier voice-and-camera AI assistant, document OCR scan-to-fill, and SHA-256 integrity-hashed certificates.

Sources: https://atteste.art/compare/artwork-artwork-alternative, https://atteste.art/compare/artwork-archive-alternative
